ShortDescription.Value: The screen as a window into your city: the camera moves with your head. Needs a head tracker and OpenTrack.

Publish.LongDescription:
HeadTrack moves the camera with your head, so the screen works like a window into the city: lean to the right and nearby towers slide left against the ground, the far hills move with you, and with a higher gain you can look around a building. It is a head-coupled perspective (an off-axis projection): the ground the camera aims at stays put, and the mouse still picks exactly what you see.
**You need** a head tracker that OpenTrack supports and OpenTrack itself. HeadTrack was built and tested with a Tobii Eye Tracker 5.
**Set up OpenTrack** - Input: your tracker. - Output: UDP over network, address 127.0.0.1, port 4242. OpenTrack's default address, 192.168.0.2, never reaches the game. - Filter: none. The mod smooths the poses itself. - Mapping: keep the translation curves 1:1. - Sit normally, facing the screen the game is on, and centre: OpenTrack's Center key, or Shift+H in the game.
**In the game:** Options, HeadTrack. Keys: Ctrl+H turns it on and off, Shift+H centres, N holds the view. Gain 1 is physically right; 3 to 5 lets you look around buildings. While you drag with a building tool the view holds still. The follow camera is on by default, photo mode off.
**Limitations** - Through OpenTrack a lost face is not seen: the view holds where your head was. - Buildings are checked with one ray along the camera's move, so on a fast turn in a narrow street the camera can touch a wall for a frame. - Level of detail and lights follow the shifted camera.
Source code, setup details and issues: https://github.com/Skyggedans/cs2-headtrack (MIT licence).
